metadata.description: Epoch-1 compile trace INDEX: the metadata half of `.vibe/trace/<run-id>/index.json` (PROP-054 `##OBS-TRACE`, the `-print-after-all` / `-time-passes` genre). It records WHAT ran, in which order, for how long and into which snapshot FILE — never an IR payload. The snapshots themselves are the one `compiler_ir/e1` documents; this record names them by relative filename and nothing else. No IR field, no trace snapshot DTO, no untyped carrier, no dependency on the compiler domain: the generated type is pure metadata. The relational laws JTD cannot express are named below in `x-relational-laws` and enforced by the hand-written validator in `vibe-wire/src/behaviour/compiler_trace_index/` (one pure pass, typed errors, no untrusted scalar cloned into a refusal); the two label sets are pinned equal by a test, so an undocumented law and an unimplemented label are both red.
x-relational-laws: schema-epoch: the root `schema` is 1 — the epoch-1 reader refuses any other number

scalar-gates: `run_id` is exactly 32 lowercase hex characters; `project.root_digest` is `sha256:` followed by exactly 64 lowercase hex characters; every free-text identity scalar (project display, scope id, scope label, artifact id, target spelling, fingerprint, pass name) is non-blank once trimmed and free of CR, LF and NUL; `project.display` is exactly `"."` in epoch 1 (the trace never leaks an absolute developer root — the outer node/unit labels live in the scopes); a CUSTOM artifact target, being an open-vocabulary spelling from a plugin, matches the same backend id charset `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}` the compiler applies to `BackendId`, while the two built-in STATIC targets satisfy it by construction
timestamp-coherence: `finished` is absent while `status` is `running`, and never earlier than `started`
scope-identity: scope ids are unique across the index, and every event's scope id names one declared scope
scope-status-coherence: a pending scope carries neither fingerprint nor failure; a compiled or skipped scope carries a fingerprint and no failure; a failed scope carries a failure and no fingerprint

skipped-scope-is-silent: a skipped scope records its fingerprint and has no pass events. ONLY `skipped` is required to be silent: a `compiled` or `failed` scope with no events is legal and says what it means — a zero-document artifact had nothing to run, or the scope failed before its first pass. The silence law exists because a SKIP is a claim that the cached fingerprint was reused; an event would contradict it

sequence-density: event sequences are dense ascending from 0 — `events[i].sequence == i` in list order. A list longer than a `uint32` can address has no dense numbering in this epoch and is refused; the position is never narrowed by a wrapping cast

invocation-key: for each (scope id, pass name) the invocation ordinals are DENSE from zero in encounter order — exactly `0..D-1`, so `parse` over D documents of one artifact numbers them `0,1,…,D-1` and every whole-artifact pass numbers `0`. Uniqueness alone would admit `0,7`, which no compiler produced; starting above zero, leaving a gap, and repeating or reordering a spent ordinal are all the same violation. The counter advances with checked addition and never wraps

shape-ladder: an input or output shape's level and cardinality follow the IR ladder — `source` is document cardinality; `document` is document or artifact; `closure`, `lane` and `emitted` are artifact

event-coherence: only `ok` names a certified snapshot; `ok` carries pass/verify/encode durations and no diagnostic; `snapshot-skipped-budget` carries pass/verify, no encode, no snapshot and no diagnostic; `pass-failed` carries only the pass duration plus a bounded diagnostic; `verification-failed` carries pass/verify plus a diagnostic; `snapshot-failed` carries pass/verify/encode plus a diagnostic and no snapshot — a failure or budget status never names a snapshot, and a missing duration is honest only where the law says so. Every duration an event does carry is CANONICAL: `saturated = true` means the true value was at least the ceiling, so it is legal only at `micros = u32::MAX`; an unsaturated `u32::MAX` stays legal, because an exact measurement may land exactly there

snapshot-portability: a snapshot filename is CONSTRUCTED from the event and its referenced scope, not merely screened by an alphabet — a name that passes a character filter but names the wrong pass, kind, label, artifact or ordinal no longer round-trips back to what wrote it, and reversibility is the point. Exactly two spellings are admitted, both one path component of at most 96 bytes: the FULL form `<seq:04>-<enc(pass)>-<kind>_<enc(scope-label)>_<enc(artifact)>-<ord:03>.json`, and the SHORT form `<seq:04>-~<digest16>-<ord:03>.json` for names the run directory's absolute path cannot afford. `enc` leaves ONLY `[A-Za-z0-9.]` raw and percent-escapes every other UTF-8 byte as uppercase `%XX` — `%`, `-`, `_`, `~`, separators, `:` and non-ASCII included — so `-` and `_` cannot occur inside a component and the layout split is total and reversible; `kind` is the referenced scope's `node|unit|publish`; the widths are Rust MINIMUM widths (zero-padded to 4 and 3, wider when the value needs it); `digest16` is the first 16 lowercase hex characters of the SHA-256 of the encoded middle `<enc(pass)>-<kind>_<enc(scope-label)>_<enc(artifact)>`, which the validator RECOMPUTES rather than accepting any `~` plus hex. The short form is legal whenever the writer chose it, because the path pressure that forces it is invisible from inside the index. Windows-safety follows rather than being enumerated: the alphabet admits no `<>:"/\|?*` and no control byte, the name begins with a digit so it cannot be a device stem, and the byte before `.json` is a digit so there is no trailing dot or space. Every other spelling — an over-encoded `%41`, a raw `-`/`_`/`~` inside a component, the wrong metadata, a two-digit ordinal, a lowercase escape, an over-96-byte name, an invented digest — is red, and the filename is unique across the run

root-coherence: the root `status` is the COMPILE/LIFECYCLE outcome, and this trace is an OBSERVER of it — the two must not be confused. A root `failure` rides only `status = failed` and `failed` carries one; `running` carries neither `finished` nor `failure`; `ok` is finished, carries no failure, no pending scope, no failed scope and no COMPILE-failed event (`pass-failed`, `verification-failed`) — a scope or pass failure hidden by root `ok` is red. A `snapshot-failed` or `snapshot-skipped-budget` event is expressly NOT a compile failure and root `ok` admits it: the observer failing to write, or standing down under budget, must never be able to turn a green run red, or `--trace-compile` would stop being a diagnostic switch. Conversely a root `failed` needs NO failed scope and NO failed event as evidence — the run may fail after every pass succeeded (the boot-artifact transaction rolling back a StaticWrite is the accepted case) — so `failed` + `finished` + a bounded `failure` is the whole obligation

aggregate-reconciliation: exactly one timing row per distinct event pass name, in FIRST-APPEARANCE order from `events` — the CLI table is a diffable artifact, so the same set of rows in a different order is red; each row's invocation count equals the event count for that pass, counted with checked arithmetic (a count past the `uint32` ceiling is refused, never wrapped); every carried total is canonical in the `event-coherence` sense before it is compared at all; each pass/verify/encode total is recomputed with checked/saturating arithmetic over the durations the events actually carry (a missing duration contributes nothing; a carried total is never trusted); a total is marked saturated when any summed duration was saturated or the sum itself overflowed, and a saturated total sits at `u32::MAX`
diagnostic-cap: every root failure, scope failure and event diagnostic is at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes (the `x-diagnostic-cap-bytes` value)

metadata.description: Index wire schema epoch; 1 in epoch 1.

The lifecycle run that owns this trace: the exact 32-lowercase-hex `RunMetadata.run_id` allocated before any compilation began. One `vibe install` (or lifecycle verb) is one run directory; the validator refuses any other spelling.
When the run began, RFC 3339. Injected like every clock here: the writer never calls `now()`, time arrives as input (PROP-044 `##M-CANONICAL-BYTES`).
Which project was compiled, without any absolute developer home path.
Terminal state of the run at the moment this index was written. `running` is a partial index captured mid-run (the final status is written last); `ok` and `failed` are final.
Every artifact compilation this run touched, in declaration order. Explicit even when empty, so a fresh `running` index is readable as `"scopes": []`.
Every pass invocation, in run order (the global `sequence` is dense from 0). Explicit even when empty.
Per-pass timing totals the CLI table prints directly. Explicit even when empty; must reconcile exactly to `events` (a carried total is never trusted).
When the run reached its terminal state; absent while `status` is `running`.

Bounded terminal diagnostic of a failed run (at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes). Present exactly when `status` is `failed`. Diagnostics are data: they may contain newlines, they never carry a provider body or secret — this schema has no such concept.
The run's terminal state. Closed: an unknown spelling is a reader error, not a newer writer — additive evolution of this record rides new object members, never new status values.
The compiled project's identity. Deliberately no absolute developer home path: `display` is the project-relative spelling (`"."` for the host root) and `root_digest` pins which tree was compiled.

Project-relative display name. Epoch 1 compiles one project per run, so the only legal spelling is `"."` — the outer node/unit labels live in the scopes, and no absolute developer path ever reaches this member.
`sha256:` followed by exactly 64 lowercase hex characters — the digest of the compiled project root.
Which kind of compilation this scope names.
Where this artifact compilation stands at the moment the index was written.

Final-artifact target identity, spelled exactly as the compiler's open target vocabulary spells it (the two built-in STATIC targets are fixed; a custom backend names itself, and the validator holds its spelling to the same `BackendId` charset the compiler would have). Duplicated from `compiler_ir/e1` by meaning, not by reference: this record carries the spelling as metadata and never the target's IR. The day the generator supports cross-schema vocabulary refs may centralize the two copies.
The IR level a pass consumed or produced — the same closed level vocabulary `compiler_ir/e1` carries, duplicated here as metadata because this record describes passes without embedding their IR.
How many values crossed one invocation: one addressed document, or one complete artifact. Same vocabulary, same meaning, same duplication ruling as `ir_level`.
The shape of one input or output value of a pass invocation.

One measured duration: microseconds plus an explicit saturation marker. `micros` saturates at u32::MAX rather than wrapping; `saturated` is true when the measurement hit that ceiling (or contributed to a total that did) — so the marker is legal ONLY at `micros = u32::MAX`, while an unsaturated `u32::MAX` stays legal because an exact measurement may land exactly there. Writer-side saturation policy lands with the recorder; the representable form is pinned here.

One artifact compilation of the run: a workspace node, a package unit, or a publish artifact. `label` is the exact unencoded outer label (the filename codec percent-encodes; the index retains the true string), `artifact` the artifact id (which repeats `static-md`/`static-xml` across scopes — the pair (`label`, `artifact`) is what disambiguates), `id` the stable scope id events reference.
Stable scope id; unique across the index, referenced by every event of this scope.
The exact unencoded node/unit label.
Artifact id, e.g. `static-md`.
Fingerprint of the compiled output; present for `compiled` and `skipped`, absent for `pending` and `failed`.
Bounded diagnostic of a failed scope; present only for `failed`.

How one pass invocation ended. Only `ok` certifies a snapshot; the two snapshot-refusals distinguish encode failure from a deliberately skipped write (budget), and the verifier half of the pipeline is reported separately from the pass body. `pass-failed` and `verification-failed` are COMPILE failures and a root `ok` refuses them; `snapshot-failed` and `snapshot-skipped-budget` are TRACE-side observability and a root `ok` admits them — the observer is not allowed to change the run's outcome.

One pass invocation: what ran (scope, pass, invocation ordinal), what it consumed and produced (input/output shapes), how it ended (status), how long each stage took (independently saturated pass/verify/encode durations — absent only where the law allows a failure to omit later stages honestly) and which certified snapshot FILE it wrote, if any. The IR itself lives in the snapshot, never here.
Dense global run sequence; `events[i].sequence == i`. Also the decimal prefix of the snapshot filename.
The scope id this invocation belongs to.
Dense invocation ordinal of THIS pass within THIS scope: encounter order is exactly `0..D-1` (parse runs per document; whole-artifact passes use 0).
Exact pass name, e.g. `parse`, `close`, `emit:static-xml`.
The shape of the value the pass consumed.
The shape of the value the pass produced.
Duration of the pass body (`PassSegment`), saturated; present whenever the body ran.
Duration of the inter-pass/semantic verification stage; present whenever the pass body succeeded (a pass with no verifier records zero, not absence).
Duration of the trace snapshot encoding, recorded separately from pass time; present exactly when an encode was attempted.

The certified snapshot's relative FILENAME — one path component, never a path, in one of the two canonical spellings `snapshot-portability` constructs: `<seq:04>-<enc(pass)>-<kind>_<enc(scope-label)>_<enc(artifact)>-<ord:03>.json`, or `<seq:04>-~<digest16>-<ord:03>.json` when the run directory cannot afford the full one. Only `ok` carries one.
Bounded diagnostic of a failed invocation; present exactly on the three failure statuses.
One row of the CLI timing table: everything the run spent on one pass name, recomputable from `events` — the validator never trusts the carried totals.
Exact pass name this row aggregates.
How many events carry this pass name.
Saturating sum of the pass durations this pass name's events carry.
Saturating sum of the verify durations.
Saturating sum of the encode durations.
